text: ‍REUTERS: Mexico's economy grows at fastest pace since late 2020 in Q2 July 30, 2026 | 🟢 📰 INEGI's official print: GDP +1.3% q/q in Q2, +2.1% y/y — the fastest pace since late 2020, above analyst forecasts, lifted by services and farming. Reuters ran it straight, no editorializing. Same outlet, one week earlier: "Mexican economy falters in May as construction dips." A bad month gets the frown; a quarter that beats expectations gets a wire brief.

🇲🇽📈 <u>HIDALGO POSTS MEXICO'S STRONGEST GROWTH: +8.16% IN 12 MONTHS</u>

INEGI's state activity indicator is out: Hidalgo grew 8.16% over the last twelve months — the fastest in Mexico, nearly three points ahead of Tamaulipas (+5.33%), with Colima in third. While most states slowed at the start of 2026, Hidalgo chained ever-stronger quarters: 2.29% in Q2 2025, 3.58% by Q4. (El Economista)

🇲🇽🤱 <u>CDMX LAUNCHES UNIVERSAL SUPPORT FOR PREGNANT WOMEN</u>

Mexico City will pay 1,200 pesos bimonthly to every pregnant woman under "Mujeres Sanas e Infancias Protegidas" — covering the full nine months, retroactively if she joins late. The target universe: more than 79,000 births a year, prioritizing zones with the highest social lag. Brugada frames it as what it is: care work recognized as a human right. The welfare state the right calls impossible keeps growing.

🇲🇽🎓 <u>MEXICAN ACADEMIA ORGANIZES TO STUDY THE FAR-RIGHT SURGE</u>

At CIDE, Mexico's public research center, scholars built REEDM — the Network for the Study of Extreme Rights in the World — an interdisciplinary project with UNAM and other institutions to explain why the far right keeps gaining ground. Secihti chief Rosaura Ruiz backs the work: studying the phenomenon "is not only legitimate, but necessary." While others normalize it, Mexican science maps it.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>WASHINGTON'S NEW ENEMY: "POLITICAL TERRORISM" — A.K.A. THE LEFT</u>

Mexico refused to attend Marco Rubio's summit — now the agenda is public. The State Department's July 2026 strategy against "political terrorism" names anticapitalists, anti-imperialists, communists, anarchists and marxists as the threat. "They can call themselves anticapitalists or anti-imperialists or communists or anarchists or marxists," Rubio said on July 16. Six decades of blockade on Cuba were the pilot program. The witch hunt is official doctrine again.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>PRI AND PAN REFUSE TO CONDEMN THE ICE KILLINGS OF MEXICANS</u>

17 Mexicans have died in ICE custody and raids since Trump returned to office. Mexico's Chamber of Deputies approved a condemnation of the violence and backed Sheinbaum's shift "from the diplomatic route to the legal and criminal one" — and PRI and PAN abstained. Their excuse: the 4T only offers "political speeches." When Mexicans are hunted abroad, the opposition can't even bring itself to say no.

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>INE ORDERS ALITO TO DELETE HIS "NARCOGOBIERNO" POSTS</u>

Mexico's electoral authority ruled unanimously against PRI boss Alejandro "Alito" Moreno: calling Morena a "narco-government" is the false accusation of a crime, not free speech. Five posts from his own accounts and four PRI reposts ordered down. The INE's complaints commission noted the slur is only shielded when made from a Senate seat under parliamentary immunity — as party propaganda, it's just defamation. The "narco-state" script is running out of legal cover.

🇲🇽📈 <u>GUELAGUETZA 2026 BREAKS RECORDS: 278,000 TOURISTS, 1,138 MILLION PESOS</u>

The Guelaguetza in Oaxaca drew more than 278,000 national and foreign tourists and left a preliminary economic spillover of 1,138 million pesos between July 1 and 27 — up 1.43% from last year, El Economista reports.

The biggest indigenous festival in Mexico just posted its best year on record.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>DEA AND PENTAGON ADMIT TRUMP BOAT STRIKES DID NOT CUT DRUG SMUGGLING</u>

The same week Stephen Miller claims cartels control Mexican territory, US agencies blow up the pretext: the DEA found the deadly boat strikes in the Caribbean and the Pacific have not reduced drug smuggling into the US — cocaine supply and price untouched, routes diversified. 215 people killed for nothing.

The Mexican answer stands: cooperation yes, subordination no.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO KEEPS THE BEST TRADE TERMS WITH THE US — EBRARD</u>

Trump says he no longer cares about renewing the T-MEC. Yet his Section 301 tariff round hit 60 countries and left Mexico untouched — no new tariffs, same preferential frame.

“If you look at the overall picture of countries, Mexico has the best deal — which also explains why our exports to the United States have grown,” Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said, confirming the next negotiating round moves to Washington in early September. Integration is leverage.
